subject: CCN
body: Which transport protocol is connection-oriented and guarantees delivery?
explanation: TCP uses a three-way handshake, sequencing and acknowledgements.

subject: CCN
body: Which transport protocol is best for live video calls where speed matters more than retransmission?
explanation: UDP has lower overhead and no retransmissions.

subject: CCN
body: What are the three steps of the TCP handshake?
explanation: This sets up a TCP connection.

subject: CCN
body: What are the four DHCP messages, in order?
explanation: Remembered as DORA.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol finds the MAC address for a known IPv4 address?
explanation: ARP maps Layer 3 addresses to Layer 2 addresses.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol does ping use?
explanation: ICMP echo request and echo reply.

subject: CCN
body: Which DNS record maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
explanation: AAAA is for IPv6; MX is for mail servers; CNAME is an alias.

subject: CCN
body: Which DNS record identifies a domain's mail server?
explanation: Mail exchanger.

subject: CCN
body: Which of these is a private IPv4 address range?

subject: CCN
body: Which address is the IPv4 loopback address?
explanation: It refers to the local device itself.

subject: CCN
body: How many bits long is an IPv4 address?
explanation: MAC addresses are 48 bits; IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

subject: CCN
body: How many bits long is an IPv6 address?
explanation: Written as eight groups of four hex digits.

subject: CCN
body: How many bits long is a MAC address?
explanation: Usually written as six pairs of hex digits.

subject: CCN
body: Which IPv6 address type starts with FE80::/10?
explanation: Link-local addresses work only on the local link.

subject: CCN
body: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
explanation: It is the IPv6 equivalent of 127.0.0.1.

subject: CCN
body: What does NAT do?
options: Translates private IP addresses to a public IP address
explanation: PAT/NAT overload lets many devices share one public address.

subject: CCN
body: Which device forwards frames using MAC addresses?
explanation: A hub repeats bits to all ports; a router forwards by IP.

subject: CCN
body: Which device connects different IP networks and chooses paths between them?
explanation: Routers use routing tables.

subject: CCN
body: What is the default gateway?
options: The router address a host uses to reach other networks
explanation: Without it, a host can only reach its local subnet.

subject: CCN
body: A VLAN is used to
options: split one physical switch into separate logical networks
explanation: Traffic between VLANs needs a router or Layer 3 switch.

subject: CCN
body: What is the maximum recommended length of a Cat6 copper Ethernet run at 1 Gbps?
explanation: Fibre is used for longer distances.

subject: CCN
body: Which cable type is immune to electromagnetic interference?
explanation: It carries light, not electricity.

subject: CCN
body: Which Wi-Fi band generally has longer range but more interference?
explanation: Higher bands are faster but have shorter range.

subject: CCN
body: Which non-overlapping channels are commonly used on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi?
explanation: Using them reduces interference.

subject: CCN
body: What is an SSID?
options: The name of a wireless network
explanation: Access points broadcast it so clients can find the network.

subject: CCN
body: Which command shows the path packets take to a destination on Windows?
explanation: On Linux/macOS it is traceroute.

subject: CCN
body: Which command tests DNS name resolution?
explanation: dig is a common alternative on Linux/macOS.

subject: CCN
body: Which Cisco IOS command gives a quick summary of interfaces, IPs and their status?
explanation: It shows each interface's up/down status.

subject: CCN
body: Which Cisco command saves the running configuration so it survives a reboot?
explanation: Often shortened to copy run start.

subject: CCN
body: A host can ping 8.8.8.8 but not google.com. What is most likely wrong?
explanation: IP connectivity works, so name resolution is the problem.

subject: CCN
body: A host has IP 192.168.1.20/24 and gateway 192.168.2.1. What is the problem?
options: The gateway is not on the host's subnet
explanation: The gateway must be in the same subnet as the host.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol should replace Telnet for remote device management?
explanation: SSH encrypts the session; Telnet sends everything in plain text.

subject: CCN
body: A firewall rule that permits traffic to TCP port 443 allows
explanation: HTTPS uses TCP 443.

subject: CCN
body: Which wireless security protocol should never be used because it is easily cracked?
explanation: WEP's encryption is broken.

subject: CCN
body: Port security on a switch is used to
options: limit which MAC addresses can use a switch port
explanation: It helps stop unauthorised devices connecting.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol synchronises device clocks across a network?
explanation: Accurate time matters for logs and authentication.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol is used to monitor and manage network devices?
explanation: Simple Network Management Protocol.

subject: CCN
body: Which protocol securely transfers files over SSH?
explanation: TFTP has no authentication or encryption.

subject: CCN
body: Which IPv4 address class has a default /8 mask?
explanation: Class B is /16 and Class C is /24 by default; Class D is multicast.

subject: CCN
body: Which IPv4 address is used to send to all hosts on the local subnet?
explanation: It is the limited broadcast address.

subject: CCN
body: How can the IPv6 address 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001 be shortened?
explanation: Drop leading zeros and replace one run of zero groups with ::.

subject: CCN
body: What does SLAAC allow an IPv6 host to do?
options: Configure its own address without a DHCP server
explanation: Stateless address autoconfiguration.

subject: CCN
body: Which device provides wireless clients with access to a wired network?
explanation: It bridges Wi-Fi and Ethernet.

subject: CCN
body: Which device converts the signal from an ISP line into Ethernet?
explanation: Modulator-demodulator.

subject: CCN
body: What does a MAC address table on a switch store?
options: Which MAC address is reachable on which port
explanation: The switch learns it from source MAC addresses.

subject: CCN
body: A cable tester shows a cable fails on several pins. Which OSI layer is the problem at?
explanation: Cabling faults are physical-layer problems.

subject: CCN
body: Which Windows command releases and renews a DHCP address?
explanation: Useful when a device has an APIPA address.

subject: CCN
body: Which command shows the ARP cache on Windows?
explanation: It lists IP-to-MAC mappings.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with cables, connectors and transmitting bits?
explanation: Layer 1 — Physical: cables, connectors and transmitting bits.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with MAC addresses, frames and switches?
explanation: Layer 2 — Data Link: MAC addresses, frames and switches.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with IP addresses, packets and routers?
explanation: Layer 3 — Network: IP addresses, packets and routers.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with TCP/UDP, segments and port numbers?
explanation: Layer 4 — Transport: TCP/UDP, segments and port numbers.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with setting up and managing sessions between applications?
explanation: Layer 5 — Session: setting up and managing sessions between applications.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with data formatting, encryption and compression?
explanation: Layer 6 — Presentation: data formatting, encryption and compression.

subject: CCN
body: Which OSI layer deals with network services used by applications, like HTTP and DNS?
explanation: Layer 7 — Application: network services used by applications, like HTTP and DNS.
